script.analysis: All 20,211 stored characters read in three contiguous ranges with canonical hash match. Hook: late-night bills at the kitchen table, not a personal failing; early subscribe/like CTA. Category tour: homeowner median monthly cost and 47% ownership-cost share, median rent $1,487 plus utilities, algorithmic rent pricing (+$800/year), homeowners-insurance increases (26 quarters, Nebraska ~$6,400), 88% insured, food 2020-2024 +23.6% versus all items 21.2%, lowest-income food share 32.6%, beef/veal +13.9%, transportation +34.4%, prescription drug spending and affordability, Q3 2024 cost-related care avoidance. Then middle-class income range $53K-$161K and Jackson/SF thresholds, first $70K derivation, median household income $83,730, generational comparison, occupational examples (teacher, nurse, police), delayed milestones, second itemized tally to $59,000 plus taxes $79,400 and add-ons to nearly $100K, close with subscribe/comment CTA. Dense statistic recitation with no sources named on most figures, no remedies and two incompatible budgets. Validating tone consistent with C1CqdnB321o. ASR artifacts ("[snorts]", "economists call trap, but for the middle class") preserved; not audio-verified.

claim_audit: 0:7000 Median rent $1,487 for 2024 resembles the ACS median gross rent, which already includes utilities; adding $200-300 utilities then double-counts if that is the source. Food 2020-2024 +23.6% versus all items +21.2% and lowest-income food share 32.6% match USDA ERS-style figures (not re-accessed). Beef/veal +13.9% "12 months ending August 2024" looks misdated; double-digit beef inflation was reported for 2025, not August 2024 - flagged, not corrected. Algorithmic pricing ~$800/year resembles a 2024 federal estimate (~$70/month) for affected units, not all renters. Homeowners insurance 26 consecutive quarters, 88% insured and transportation +34.4% unverified here.

7000:14000 First tally: housing $21,000 (stated to include insurance and utilities) + insurance $1,750-2,500 again + transport $11,000 + food $8,000 + healthcare $3,000 + other $4,000 = ~$48,750-$49,500; take-home on $70K stated $52K-$55K, so this tally leaves ~$2.5K-$6K, contradicting "zero cushion", and double-counts insurance. Middle-class $53K-$161K resembles Pew Research thresholds (a think-tank definition for a household size), not "government statistics". Median household income 2024 $83,730 matches the Census release. US prescription spending ">$600 billion" depends on definition (retail vs total); affordability survey figures (1 in 4, ~30% rationing, Q3 2024 8%/7%/6%) unverified.

14000:20211 Second tally sums to $59,400 (script "$59,000") with higher category values than the first tally and separate car insurance and utilities already included earlier. Adding $15,000 income tax + $5,350 FICA on $70K gives ~$79,400-79,750, which means $70K would not cover the listed costs - the headline "$70K survival" is contradicted by the script's own math. FICA 7.65% x $70,000 = $5,355, correct. Car payment >$700 average applies to financed new cars, not every household; adding car payments after "transportation $12,000" double-counts. Occupational salaries ($55K teacher, $62K nurse, $58K police) unsourced and below commonly reported national medians for nurses.
